item.title: GNU Bison
item.description:
GNU Bison generates parsers from context-free grammars. Its Yacc-compatible notation defines tokens, nonterminals, semantic values, and actions; the generated parser obtains tokens from a scanner by convention. Consult the GNU Bison manual for skeleton- and language-specific interfaces.

Grammar Sections, Values, and Actions #

A grammar has declarations, productions, and optional epilogue code, separated by %%. Declarations define tokens, value types, precedence, parser settings, and required code. Productions define nonterminals and actions.

item.title: Formal Languages and Parsing
item.description:
A formal language is a set of finite strings over an alphabet. A grammar defines productions that derive strings in that set. Compiler front ends use this model to separate local token recognition from recursive program structure.

Chomsky Families #

The Chomsky hierarchy classifies grammars by production restrictions:

  1. Type 3, regular grammars, describe regular languages recognized by finite automata. Regular expressions and lexers operate here.
  2. Type 2, context-free grammars (CFGs), have one nonterminal on the left of each production and are recognized by pushdown automata.
  3. Type 1, context-sensitive grammars, restrict productions so they do not shorten sentential forms except for defined start-symbol cases.
  4. Type 0, unrestricted grammars, impose no comparable production restriction.

Balanced delimiters illustrate the boundary. A finite automaton cannot remember an unbounded nesting depth, whereas a CFG can use recursion such as Group → '(' Group ')' Group | ε.

item.title: LR Parsing
item.description:
LR parsing is a table-driven bottom-up method for deterministic context-free grammars. L means tokens are read left to right; R means the parser constructs a rightmost derivation in reverse.

Shift-Reduce Machine #

The parser maintains a stack of states and grammar symbols. For each state and lookahead token, an action table chooses one of:

  1. Shift: consume the token and push the destination state.
  2. Reduce: replace the right-hand side of a production with its left-hand-side nonterminal, then use the goto table to select the next state.
  3. Accept: recognize the augmented start production at end of input.
  4. Error: report that no valid continuation exists.
text 
push state 0
repeat
 action = ACTION[top_state, lookahead]
 if action is shift s: consume lookahead; push s
 if action is reduce A → β: pop |β| grammar symbols and states; push GOTO[top_state, A]
 if action is accept: return syntax tree
 otherwise: report a syntax error

Semantic actions commonly run on reduction. A parallel value stack stores AST nodes or other values for the symbols being reduced.
